FRadioPlayer 0.4.0 adopts Swift 6 and main-actor isolation, and fixes playback intent, callback delivery, and audio-session configuration. **This release has source and behavior changes for apps upgrading from 0.3.x.**

## Requirements

iOS 14+, macOS 11+, tvOS 14+, and Xcode 16+ (Swift 6 toolchain). The package builds in Swift 6 mode; consuming apps can remain in Swift 5 mode. Platform minimums are unchanged.

## Migrating from 0.3.x

- `FRadioPlayer` is `@MainActor`. Controllers that call the player must run on the main actor, including in Swift 5 apps. Add `@MainActor` to the controller, or use `Task { @MainActor in ... }` from a nonisolated context.
- `FRadioPlayerObserver` callbacks run on the main actor. Declaring the conformance on a class infers main-actor isolation. Its `@preconcurrency` annotation preserves compatibility for existing conformers.
- `seek(to:completion:)` preserves playback intent. A paused or stopped player stays paused or stopped. Call `play()` explicitly if your UI intends to resume after seeking.
- Update a dependency constrained to the 0.3 minor series, such as `.upToNextMinor(from: "0.3.0")`, to the 0.4 series. An exact 0.3 pin also needs updating.

```swift
@MainActor
final class RadioController {
    let player = FRadioPlayer.shared

    func play(_ url: URL) {
        player.radioURL = url
        player.play()
    }
}
```

Apps that own their audio session can opt out **before the first access to `shared`**, from the main actor:

```swift
FRadioPlayer.configuresAudioSession = false
```

The default is `true`. The library sets the category but never activates or deactivates the session. Changing this flag after the singleton exists has no effect.

## Playback and audio fixes

- Seek completions run exactly once, asynchronously on the main actor, including when there is no loaded player, no known duration, or a superseded seek. A pause or stop while seeking wins over an earlier play intent. Seek positions retain subsecond precision.
- Interruptions resume only playback that was active when the interruption began, only when the system allows resumption, and only if the user has not since paused or stopped.
- Rebuilding a failed stream no longer passes the redundant explicit `AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: false` option that prevented recovery in iOS 27 validation. Custom HTTP header options remain supported by the existing asset setup.
- A failed load reports `.error` without a transient `.loadingFinished` notification.
- Late artwork results from a previous station or track are discarded.
- The default audio session now uses valid `.playback` category options. Removing incompatible explicit route options fixes category setup failures observed on a physical iPhone.
- Losing an audio route continues to pause playback; the ineffective headphones check was removed.

## Concurrency

- AVFoundation, audio-session, network, and artwork callbacks cross to the main actor before changing player state. Off-main KVO is reduced to Sendable values before the hop; late events from replaced items are ignored.
- Metadata delivery uses the main queue explicitly registered with AVFoundation. `FRadioPlayer.Metadata` remains non-Sendable because it carries `AVTimedMetadataGroup` values; keep it on the main actor.
- `FRadioPlayer.State`, `FRadioPlayer.PlaybackState`, and `iTunesAPI` are `Sendable`. Artwork-provider completions are `@Sendable` and may be invoked on any queue; existing provider conformances remain compatible.
- Library sources use neither `@unchecked Sendable` nor `nonisolated(unsafe)`.

## Demo and validation

- The SwiftUI demo controller and remote-command handlers use main-actor isolation.
- The demo includes the new app icon and replaces the unavailable Classic Rock stream with Choice Classic Rock.
- CI covers macOS tests, iOS simulator tests, the Swift 5 demo consumer, and a build with the minimum Xcode 16 toolchain.

Simulator tests cover playback intent, interruption and route-change notifications, seek completion, stale artwork, failed-stream recovery, and callback delivery. Physical audio routing remains a device-level check.
